title: Gallium is a metal that can melt in a warm hand
body: Pure gallium melts at about **29.8°C**, only a little above a typical room temperature. A sufficiently warm hand can transfer enough heat to turn a small solid piece into liquid metal. Melting changes how its atoms are arranged and move; it does not turn gallium into a different substance. The dramatic change is a physical change of state.

slides.question: At what temperature does pure gallium melt?
slides.explanation: About 29.8 °C, roughly 85.6 °F, only a little above room temperature, which is why a warm hand can turn a small piece into liquid metal.

slides.label: Approximate melting point of pure gallium
slides.text: That is about 85.6°F, far below the temperatures needed to melt familiar metals such as iron.

slides.heading: Where the heat comes from
slides.text: Heat flows from a warmer hand into cooler gallium. Once the metal reaches its melting point, more heat can turn solid gallium into liquid.

left.label: Solid gallium
left.text: Its atoms form an ordered structure.

right.label: Liquid gallium
right.text: Its atoms can move past one another. They are still gallium atoms.
